analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen-missing-user-query-400.md) and edits to docs/architecture/inference.md (header date; a new paragraph in the 'Chat-template render check' section near base line 715; a new failure-mode table row near base line 1116). The docs describe an unseen code change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Prompting/Qwen35TemplateFixes.swift (`validateUserQuery`). That change reclassifies Qwen 3.5/3.6/3.8 and Bonsai 2 histories with no user turn beyond `<tool_response>` wrappers. They are now refused before rendering with typed HTTP 400 `missingUserQuery` instead of provider 500 `template_render`. No Swift source is in this batch, so the validation logic itself was not reviewed. Coverage limit: I could not verify that the check runs before model acquisition, that it correctly handles multimodal user content (image/video-only user turns), or that the 400 error body does not echo prompt content. Prompt content is A-001; T-008 and TB-002 are relevant if the error path leaks it. A false-positive 400 could affect availability for legitimate requests. A 400 versus 500 distinction may also affect coordinator reroute or provider-fault accounting in the platform-owned backend, which is out of scope. Nothing in the docs touches the encryption, attestation, authorization or prefix-cache boundaries, such as T-041. No security regression is evidenced by the documentation alone. Integration should confirm the Swift diff if it is in another batch. In particular, it should check that the validation runs only on already-decrypted in-process data, that no plaintext appears in the error, and that the 400 cannot be triggered by crafted content to bypass the `template_render_ok` capacity gate.
